value:
PER-SITE FORM-CLASS TAXONOMY of the six suspected form-class residuals, measured 2026-09-01, for lane LZ's equivalent_copy_form rule. CLASSES: (a) unconditional mr<->addi-copy, rS!=r0, no dataflow obligation; (b) li-vs-copy, needs a dominating-def proof; (c) NOT the form class. HEADLINE: the roster yields ZERO class-(a) sites and exactly THREE class-(b) sites, all three inside ONE function; every other measured site is (c), and in every (c) case the disqualifier is the instruction COUNT, not the register theory. LZ's v1 unconditional rule therefore gains NO new customers from this roster beyond CTriListCollide - but the (b) rule, if built, gets three sites with unusually clean preconditions.

=== CLASS (b): G3DReadControlPadStates, game/g3d/gcontrolpads, 48/48 insns, real 20, multiset DIFFERS target-only +2 addi +1 mr / ours-only -3 li. All three sites share ONE source register, r29, defined ONCE by `li r29,0` (target 0x14, ours 0x18). Site B1 @0x1c: target `mr r30,r29`, ours `li r30,0`. The def is the IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING instruction in our stream (0x18), straight-line, no interposed write to r29, no interposed branch target, no interposed call. This is the cheapest dominating-def obligation in the whole family - a one-instruction backward scan discharges it - and is the site to build the (b) audit against FIRST. Site B2 @0x38: target `addi r7,r29,0`, ours `li r7,0`. Site B3 @0x3c: target `addi r3,r29,0`, ours `li r3,0`. B2 and B3 share one extra obligation B1 does not have: `bl G3DGetPadStatusBuffer` sits at 0x24, BETWEEN the def at 0x18 and the uses at 0x38/0x3c. r29 is non-volatile (r14-r31) so the PPC EABI guarantees the callee preserves it, but that is an ABI argument, not a local-scan argument - a purely syntactic backward scan MUST either model callee-saved registers explicitly or refuse any window containing a `bl`. Recommend v1 refuse bl-crossing windows (which passes B1, defers B2/B3) rather than encode an ABI assumption into a fail-closed guard. BRANCH-TARGET AUDIT, run in full: the only branch targets in the function are 0x44 (the bdnz loop head), 0x70, 0x7c, 0x80 and 0xa0 - ALL at or after 0x44, so all three sites sit in the straight-line preheader and no back-edge can re-enter between the def and any use. r29 IS re-written inside the loop (`or r29,r29,r6` at 0x7c) but no path leads from there back to 0x38.

ECONOMIC WARNING for LZ, and the most important operational finding in this record: closing all three (b) sites does NOT make G3DReadControlPadStates exact. Two independent non-form residuals survive. (i) A SCHEDULE swap of two adjacent independent instructions at 0x14/0x18: target emits `li r29,0` then `addi r31,r3,LO`, ours emits them in the opposite order. The prior record calls this a knock-on of the form difference; that reading is plausible but the swap is a genuine permutation and the rule will still have to account for it. (ii) A pure r6<->r8 RECOLOR: target `addi r8,r31,8` @0x28 and `srw r6,r5,r7` @0x4c, ours `addi r6,r31,8` and `srw r8,r5,r7`, with the knock-on at `lwz r4,0(rX)` @0x44 and `or r29,r29,rX` @0x7c/0x84. So this function needs a COMPOSED form+permute+recolor rule, i.e. exactly the composition that claim.parked.mbrendertext-color-tiebreak reports does not exist today and that lane RQ is separately pricing for StartThrowMagicFX. Price the composition BEFORE promising this function as a matched% win; the (b) audit alone buys three rows out of twenty, not the function.

=== CLASS (c), five sites, all disqualified on COUNT before any register theory. C1 CritterMoveSetup, game/enemy/critter, 77/76, real 7, multiset DIFFERS target-only +1 b +1 bge / ours-only -1 blt. DIRECT ANSWER TO THE LANE'S QUESTION - NO, the retained real-7 state's residual is NOT the form pair. Aligned read @0xc0:0x100: the ENTIRE residual is one target-only instruction, the empty-block forward unfused pair `bge ->0xd8` + `b ->0xf4` at 0xd0/0xd4 where we emit the single fused `blt ->0xf0`; every other row in the window is byte-identical modulo the uniform -4 shift, including the `mr r0,r4`/`mr r4,r0` copy pair at 0xec/0xf0 which is present and IDENTICAL on both sides. Target-longer by one: ineligible for any form-rewrite rule, which substitutes but cannot insert. C2 CritterAnimate, same TU, 188/188, real 38, cluster @0x60: the SAME empty-block forward-pair shape, target `blt ->0x68` + `b ->0x6c` against our fused `bge ->0x68`, target-longer by one. C3 CritterAnimate cluster @0x140-0x14c: this one LOOKS like the family and is not. Target materializes ONE zero, `li r4,0` @0x144, and feeds it to BOTH `xor r3,r6,r4` and `xor r0,r5,r4`; ours materializes TWO, `li r4,0` @0x140 and `li r0,0` @0x144, one per xor, and the knock-on is `xor r0,r5,r0`. This is the live-zero family in the OURS-LONGER direction - closing it requires DELETING an instruction and recoloring, which is the one thing the count laws place permanently outside WebFrank. Recommend LZ record the family as having two sub-populations with opposite dispositions: count-symmetric li->copy (rewritable, the B-sites) and count-asymmetric remat-vs-CSE (never rewritable, C3 and the CritterAnimate/MapMusicStart end of the list). The two are easy to confuse from an --ops line alone because both report `ours-only -N li`. C4 GetEnemyType, game/game/gamemain, 61/59: the run-13 park's diagnosis is CONFIRMED verbatim from the bytes - target home-copies both incoming parameters, `addi r5,r3,0` @0x4 and `addi r6,r4,0` @0x10, and our stream emits neither. NOTE THE TRAP FOR THIS LANE SPECIFICALLY: these two target instructions ARE addi-copies with rS!=r0, so a naive opcode-pair scan will flag this function as prime class-(a) material. It is not: they are target-ONLY instructions, not the target half of a form pair, and the genuine form row @0x1c (target `addi r31,r5,0` vs ours `addi r31,r3,0`) is form-IDENTICAL on both sides and differs only in register - a recolor knock-on of the missing copies. C5 fn_80051C78, same TU, 105/103: park CONFIRMED and it is not the class. Its three add-plus-displacement versus addi-plus-x-form clusters @0x28, @0x138 and @0x164 are genuine opcode differences in the addressing shape, and the apparent li row @0x14c is a mis-pairing artifact - the aligned read shows target `addi r7,r3,0` (a copy of the fn_800511D0 call result) @0x14c and a separate target-only `li r3,0` @0x15c against our `li r6,0`/`li r4,0`, i.e. the target keeps the call result and the loop index in different registers where we reuse one. Count-asymmetric and structural.

=== NOT MEASURED. show_gold, game/shop/shop.c: SKIPPED by ownership, not by evidence - shop.c is lane SP's this run. Recorded here so the next pass does not read this taxonomy as covering it.

=== RECORD DISCREPANCY, reported per the step-zero duty. attempt.crittermovesetup-forward-branch-pair-costs-ternary-result-register.20260831.v1 states its probe 3, the arm-swapped ternary, reached 77/77 with an IDENTICAL opcode multiset at real 18. That state was NOT reproducible this session from the record's prose. Both arm orders were built and measured: `(nodeIndex < 0) ? node : ((candidate = X) != NULL ? candidate : node)` gives 77/78, multiset 3t, real 13; the natural order gives 77/78, multiset 5t, real 13. Neither is count-symmetric and neither reaches 0t - both are OURS-longer, where the record's state was equal-length. The park's CONCLUSION is unaffected and stands (the axis is dead either way, and both probes regressed against the retained real 7), but its 77/77-multiset-0t state should not be relied on as an existing count-symmetric, WebFrank-eligible state of this function: no such state was reachable from the two spellings the record's own description admits. If a future lane wants that state it must be re-derived, not quoted. The likely cause is that the record's probe 3 embedded the inner NULL test as a statement or comma-expression rather than as a nested ternary, a detail its prose does not preserve - which is itself an argument for recording the exact probed source form, not a paraphrase of it.
